Prealgebra · Lesson 7.3

Unit Rates and Speed

Solve this lesson →All lessons

A rate compares two quantities in different units, like dollars per pound or miles per hour. The word per signals a rate. A unit rate is the per-one value, how much of the first thing goes with exactly one unit of the second.

Problem
Dried cherries cost 20 dollars for 4 pounds. What is the price per pound, in dollars?
Show a hint
  • The sign packs four pounds together into one price. To find what just one pound costs, share the 2020 dollars equally among the 44 pounds.
  • Divide the dollars by the pounds, 20 dollars4 pounds4 pounds20 dollars​. That single quotient is the price for one pound.
Show the full solution
Divide the dollars by the pounds. 20 dollars4 pounds=54 pounds20 dollars​=5 dollars per pound, so one pound costs 55​ dollars. A unit rate is always the first quantity divided by the second, which here splits the total price evenly across the pounds.
Problem
A reader finishes a 426-page novel in 6 days at a steady pace. How many pages per day did she read?
Show a hint
  • A unit rate is the amount that goes with one of the second quantity. Here the second quantity is days, so you want the pages that go with one day. That means sharing all the pages equally among the 6 days.
  • Divide the total pages by the number of days. Compute 426÷6426÷6, and the result is the pages she reads each day.
Show the full solution
Divide the pages by the days. 426 pages6 days=71 pages per day6 days426 pages​=71 pages per day So she read 7171​ pages per day. Going backward checks it, since 71×6=42671×6=426 pages, the whole novel.
Problem
Two olive-oil bottles: 15 oz for $6.00$6.00, or 24 oz for $8.40$8.40. Find the price per ounce of each and identify the better buy. What is the price per ounce of the better buy, in dollars?
Show a hint
  • A unit rate is a cost for one of something. For each bottle, divide the total dollars by the number of ounces to get dollars for one ounce. Do this twice, once per bottle.
  • First bottle: $6.0015 oz=$0.4015 oz$6.00​=$0.40 per ounce. Second bottle: $8.4024 oz=$0.3524 oz$8.40​=$0.35 per ounce. The better buy is the smaller of these two numbers.
Show the full solution
Divide dollars by ounces for each bottle. First bottle, $6.0015 oz=$0.4015 oz$6.00​=$0.40 per ounce. Second bottle, $8.4024 oz=$0.3524 oz$8.40​=$0.35 per ounce. The second bottle is cheaper per ounce, so it is the better buy at 0.350.35​ dollars per ounce. The larger total price does not settle a best buy, only the price for one unit does.
Problem
Printer A outputs 1,800 pages in 40 minutes. Printer B outputs 1,450 pages in 25 minutes. Find each printer's pages-per-minute rate. What is the rate of the faster printer?
Show a hint
  • The page totals are over different times, so you cannot compare them head to head yet. Knock each printer down to one minute first. For each printer divide its pages by its minutes.
Show the full solution
Divide pages by minutes for each printer. Printer A, 1,800 pages40 minutes=4540 minutes1,800 pages​=45 pages per minute. Printer B, 1,450 pages25 minutes=5825 minutes1,450 pages​=58 pages per minute. Printer B is faster, at 5858​ pages per minute. The raw page totals cannot be compared until both machines are measured over the same single minute.
Key idea
A rate compares two quantities in different units, and the word per marks one, as in dollars per pound, pages per day, miles per hour. The unit rate is the per-one version, so divide the first quantity by the second to get the amount for one unit. 20 dollars4 pounds=5 dollars per pound4pounds20dollars​=5 dollars per pound Unit rates also compare prices. Write each option as a price for one unit, and the lower price per unit is the better buy, even when that option costs more in total.
Problem
A drive covers 195 miles in 3 hours at a steady pace. What is the speed in miles per hour?
Show a hint
  • The unit miles per hour is a recipe. It says take the miles and divide by the hours, which lands you on the miles covered in one hour.
  • Compute 195÷3195÷3. That tells you how many miles fit into each single hour of driving.
Show the full solution
Divide the miles by the hours. 195 miles3 hours=65 miles per hour3 hours195 miles​=65 miles per hour The speed is 6565​ miles per hour. The unit names the operation, since miles per hour means miles divided by hours.
Problem
A van cruises at 48 miles per hour for 7 hours straight. How many miles did it travel?
Show a hint
  • Speed tells you the miles gained in one hour. To get the miles for all the hours, you do not divide here, you build up, so distance is speed times time.
  • Multiply the 4848 miles in each hour by the 77 hours the van kept driving.
Show the full solution
Distance is speed times time, so 48mileshour×7 hours=33648hourmiles​×7 hours=336 miles. The van covered 336336​ miles. The hours in the rate cancel the hours of driving and leave plain miles, the unit a distance should have.
Problem
An e-bike can hold 56 mph on a 392-mile route. How many hours does the ride take?
Show a hint
  • Speed connects distance, time, and miles per hour. You have the distance and the speed, so flip the relationship around. Time is distance divided by speed.
  • Each hour covers 56 miles, so count how many 56 mile chunks fit in 392 miles. Compute 392÷56392÷56.
Show the full solution
Time is distance divided by speed, so 392 miles56 miles per hour=756 miles per hour392 miles​=7 hours. The ride takes 77​ hours. Running it forward checks the answer, since 56×7=39256×7=392 miles.
Problem
A scooter covers 21 miles in 45 minutes. Convert 45 minutes to hours first, then find the speed in miles per hour.
Show a hint
  • The unit you want is miles per hour, so the time underneath the miles has to be in hours, not minutes. Turn 45 minutes into a fraction of an hour first by writing it over the 60 minutes in one hour.
  • You have 4560=346045​=43​ of an hour, which is 0.750.75 hours. Now divide the distance by that time, 21÷0.7521÷0.75, and the result comes out in miles per hour.
Show the full solution
Put the time in hours first. 4545 minutes is 4560=346045​=43​ of an hour, which is 0.750.75 hours. Now divide. 21 miles0.75 hours=28 miles per hour0.75 hours21 miles​=28 miles per hour The speed is 2828​ miles per hour. Miles per hour needs hours underneath the miles, so leaving the time in minutes gives the wrong number.
Problem
A commuter train travels at 64 mph for 105 minutes. Convert 105 minutes to hours, then find the distance in miles.
Show a hint
  • The speed is per hour, so the time must be in hours too. Turn 105105 minutes into hours by dividing by 6060, since one hour is 6060 minutes. You should get 10560=1.7560105​=1.75 hours.
  • Now that the units match, use distance == speed ×× time. Multiply 6464 miles per hour by 1.751.75 hours and watch the "hours" cancel, leaving miles.
Show the full solution
The speed is per hour, so convert the time. 105 minutes=10560 hours=1.75 hours105 minutes=60105​ hours=1.75 hours Then use distance == speed ×× time. 64mileshour×1.75 hours=112 miles64hourmiles​×1.75 hours=112 miles The train traveled 112112​ miles. The hours cancel and leave miles, which is the check that the units were set up right.
Key idea
Speed is distance ÷ time. Whatever comes before per is what you measured, and whatever comes after is what you divide by, so miles per hour means mileshourshoursmiles​. The three quantities are one fact written three ways. s=dt,d=s×t,t=dss=td​,d=s×t,t=sd​ In the triangle, cover the one you want. If it is on top, multiply the other two, and if it is under the line, divide. Make the units match first. A speed in miles per hour needs its time in hours, so divide minutes by 60 (45 minutes =0.75=0.75 hour).
Problem
A road trip has two legs: 84 miles in 2 hours, then 161 miles in 3 hours. What is the average speed for the whole trip in miles per hour?
Show a hint
  • Average speed is not the average of the two separate speeds. It is the total distance you traveled divided by the total time you spent. First add up all the miles, then add up all the hours.
  • The miles add to 84+161=24584+161=245 miles and the hours add to 2+3=52+3=5 hours. Now divide the total distance by the total time, 245÷5245÷5.
Show the full solution
Add the miles, add the hours, then divide. The trip covers 84+161=24584+161=245 miles in 2+3=52+3=5 hours, so 245 miles5 hours=49 miles per hour.5 hours245 miles​=49 miles per hour. The average speed is 4949​ miles per hour. Averaging the leg speeds of 4242 and about 53.753.7 would give something else, because the two legs took different amounts of time.
Problem
A courier rides 210 miles out at 30 mph (headwind) and 210 miles back at 70 mph (tailwind). The simple midpoint of 50 mph is wrong. What is the average speed for the whole round trip?
Show a hint
  • Average speed is never the average of the two speeds. It is total distance divided by total time, so your first job is to find each leg's time. For the trip out, time is distance divided by speed, which is 210 miles30 miles per hour30 miles per hour210 miles​. Do the same for the trip back at 7070 miles per hour.
  • The trip out takes 21030=730210​=7 hours and the trip back takes 21070=370210​=3 hours, so the total time is 1010 hours. The total distance is the two equal legs added together, 210+210=420210+210=420 miles. Now divide 420420 miles by 1010 hours.
Show the full solution
Find each leg's time with time equals distance divided by speed. The leg out takes 21030=730210​=7 hours and the leg back takes 21070=370210​=3 hours, so the round trip is 420420 miles in 1010 hours. 420 miles10 hours=42 miles per hour10 hours420 miles​=42 miles per hour The average speed is 4242​ miles per hour. It sits below 5050 because 77 of the 1010 hours were spent on the slow leg.
Key idea
Average speed over a whole trip is the total distance divided by the total time. It is the single steady speed that would cover the same trip in the same time. It is almost never the average of the leg speeds, because you spend more time at the slower speed, so that leg counts for more. Add up every mile and every hour first, then divide.
Fun fact
Ship speed is measured in knots, one knot is one nautical mile per hour. The name comes from sailors counting knots on a rope timed with a sandglass. A knot is itself a unit rate.
Problem
Two trucks 300 miles apart drive toward each other at 45 mph and 55 mph. How many hours until they meet?
Show a hint
  • You do not have to track each truck on its own. Think about the gap between them. Every hour it gets smaller by both speeds added together, so the gap closes at 45+5545+55 miles per hour.
  • Once you know how fast the gap closes, treat it like any time question. Time equals the distance to close divided by the closing speed, so divide the 300300 mile gap by that combined speed.
Show the full solution
The gap closes at the combined speed, 45+55=10045+55=100 miles per hour. The gap starts at 300300 miles, so they meet after 300 miles100 miles per hour=3100 miles per hour300 miles​=3​ hours. Watching the gap is easier than tracking each truck, and the check works, since 45×3=13545×3=135 and 55×3=16555×3=165 add to 300300 miles.
Key idea
Two movers heading toward each other. Instead of tracking each one, watch the gap between them. Both movers shorten that gap at the same time, so it shrinks at the combined speed, the two speeds added together. The time until they meet is the starting gap divided by that combined speed.

Practice these ideas

Practice
A fruit cart sells 7 pounds of apples for 28 dollars. What is the price per pound, in dollars?
Show the solution
Divide the dollars by the pounds. 28 dollars7 pounds=47 pounds28 dollars​=4, so one pound costs 44​ dollars. Every pound costs the same, so splitting the total evenly across the pounds gives the price of one.
Practice
A resting heart beats 312 times in 4 minutes. What is the heart rate in beats per minute?
Show the solution
Divide the beats by the minutes. 312 beats4 minutes=78 beats per minute4 minutes312 beats​=78 beats per minute The heart rate is 7878​ beats per minute.
Practice
Two bags of brown rice: 12 oz for $3.60$3.60, or 20 oz for $5.00$5.00. Find the price per ounce of each and identify the better buy. What is that price per ounce, in dollars?
Show the solution
Turn each bag into a price for one ounce by dividing the cost by the number of ounces. The smaller bag gives $3.6012 ounces=$0.3012 ounces$3.60​=$0.30 per ounce. The larger bag gives $5.0020 ounces=$0.2520 ounces$5.00​=$0.25 per ounce. Now compare. Since 0.250.25 is less than 0.300.30, the larger bag is the better buy, and its price per ounce is 0.250.25​ dollars.
Practice
Machine A makes 240 parts in 8 hours. Machine B makes 350 parts in 10 hours. What is the rate of the faster machine, in parts per hour?
Show the solution
Find the unit rate for each machine by dividing its parts by its hours. For machine A, 240 parts8 hours=308 hours240 parts​=30 parts per hour. For machine B, 350 parts10 hours=3510 hours350 parts​=35 parts per hour. Now compare the two per-hour numbers. Machine B makes 35 parts every hour and machine A makes only 30, so machine B is the faster one. Its rate is 3535​ parts per hour.
Practice
A commuter train covers 280 miles in 5 hours at a steady pace. What is the train's speed in miles per hour?
Show the solution
Divide the distance by the time. 280 miles5 hours=56 miles per hour5 hours280 miles​=56 miles per hour The train's speed is 5656​ miles per hour. A quick check, 56×5=28056×5=280 miles, matches the distance given.
Practice
A maglev shuttle holds a steady 62 miles per hour for 4 hours. How many miles does it travel?
Show the solution
Distance is speed times time. 62 miles per hour×4 hours=248 miles62 miles per hour×4 hours=248 miles The shuttle covers 248248​ miles. The hours cancel against the hours in the rate, leaving miles.
Practice
A tour bus has 414 miles ahead and cruises at 46 miles per hour. How many hours does the trip take?
Show the solution
Time is distance divided by speed. time=414 miles46 miles per hour=9 hourstime=46 miles per hour414 miles​=9 hours The trip takes 99​ hours. The miles cancel against the miles in "miles per hour" and leave hours, exactly the unit we want.
Practice
A cyclist covers 35 miles in 50 minutes. Convert 50 minutes to hours (5665​ hr), then find the speed in miles per hour.
Show the solution
First put the time into hours. Fifty minutes is 5060=566050​=65​ of an hour. Speed is distance divided by time, so 35 miles56 hour=35×65=2105=42 miles per hour.65​ hour35 miles​=35×56​=5210​=42 miles per hour. The speed is 4242​.
Practice
A survey drone flies at 72 mph for 25 minutes. Convert 25 minutes to hours first, then find the distance covered in miles.
Show the solution
The speed is given per hour, so first change 2525 minutes into hours. One hour is 6060 minutes, so 2525 minutes is 2560=5126025​=125​ of an hour. Distance is speed times time, so 72 miles per hour×512 hour=72×512=36012=3072 miles per hour×125​ hour=1272×5​=12360​=30 miles. The drone covers 3030​ miles.
Practice
A scooter rides at 36 mph to a drop-off 9 miles away. Find the travel time in minutes.
Show the solution
Start with time equals distance divided by speed. The distance is 99 miles and the speed is 3636 miles per hour, so the time in hours is 9 miles36 miles per hour=14 hour.36 miles per hour9 miles​=41​ hour. Now turn that quarter of an hour into minutes. One hour is 6060 minutes, so multiply. 14 hour×60 minutes per hour=15 minutes.41​ hour×60 minutes per hour=15 minutes. The trip takes 1515​ minutes.
Practice
A van drives two legs: 90 miles in 2 hours through hills, then 140 miles in 3 hours on the highway. What is the average speed for the whole route in miles per hour?
Show the solution
Add the miles, add the hours, then divide. The route is 90+140=23090+140=230 miles in 2+3=52+3=5 hours, so 230 miles5 hours=46 miles per hour.5 hours230 miles​=46 miles per hour. The average speed is 4646​ miles per hour. The mean of the leg speeds would give 45564565​ instead, since the van spent different amounts of time on each leg.
Practice
A kayaker paddles 60 miles upstream at 20 mph, then 60 miles downstream at 30 mph. The simple midpoint of 25 mph is wrong. What is the average speed for the whole round trip?
Show the solution
Find each leg's time with time equals distance divided by speed. Upstream takes 60 miles20 miles per hour=320 miles per hour60 miles​=3 hours and downstream takes 60 miles30 miles per hour=230 miles per hour60 miles​=2 hours, so the round trip is 120120 miles in 55 hours. That gives 120 miles5 hours=245 hours120 miles​=24​ miles per hour. It lands below the midpoint of 2525 because the slow upstream leg took more of the clock.
Practice
Two drones start from opposite ends of a 264-mile tunnel and fly toward each other at 38 mph and 50 mph. How many hours until they meet?
Show the solution
The gap closes at the combined speed, 38+50=8838+50=88 miles per hour. The tunnel is 264264 miles long, so they meet after 264 miles88 miles per hour=388 miles per hour264 miles​=3​ hours. Checking, the drones cover 38×3=11438×3=114 miles and 50×3=15050×3=150 miles, which add to the full 264264.
Practice
Two cyclists start 350 miles apart and pedal toward each other at 30 mph and 40 mph. Find when they meet, then calculate how far the faster cyclist has traveled.
Show the solution
The gap closes at the combined speed, 30+40=7030+40=70 miles per hour, so the cyclists meet after 350 miles70 miles per hour=570 miles per hour350 miles​=5 hours. The faster cyclist rides 40×5=20040×5=200​ miles. As a check, the slower one covers 30×5=15030×5=150 miles, and 200+150=350200+150=350 miles, the whole starting gap.
